notes: Retains same-module imports cleanly, but the ownership map still discards valid child instance imports before expansion, and the fixture incorrectly enshrines that resource-wide suppression.

Fixes multiple same-module imports with useful count and module coverage, but still drops non-overlapping child imports at configuration-resource granularity and explicitly tests that incorrect behavior.

Fixes the reported reproduction, but parent imports still suppress every child import for the configuration resource rather than resolving precedence per expanded instance, which the new test does not cover.

The focused regression test verifies the basic fix, but configuration-resource ownership still silently removes non-overlapping child imports instead of applying parent precedence only to matching expanded instances.
Fixes the basic reproduction but retains premature resource-wide suppression of child imports and introduces an unnecessary quadratic scan, while testing only the straightforward same-module case.

Preserves multiple same-module imports, but the ownership filter still drops legitimate child imports for other resource or module instances, and the regression test does not exercise that expansion-sensitive behavior.
Provides consistent delimiter predicates and useful nested-block/dispenser coverage, but preserves—and explicitly tests—the incorrect rejection of quoted '{' in an address list.
Uses clean token-level predicates and broad parser/dispenser regression coverage, but quoted addresses ending in '{' and directive-boundary handling for quoted '{}' remain incorrect.
Handles directive, nested-block, and import delimiter checks with useful regression tests, but retains the quote-blind address-suffix check and incorrect directive-boundary handling for quoted '{}'.
Fixes the main parser/dispenser paths with useful token-level tests, but quoted brace import-mapping keys and quoted addresses ending in '{' still encounter quote-blind checks.
Fixes directive and dispenser nesting, but leaves address/import-key checks quote-blind, unnecessarily duplicates parser/dispenser helpers, and adds only weak parsed-output assertions.
Fixes ordinary quoted-brace arguments and nesting, but leaves address/import-key checks and ArgErr quote-blind and adds no dispenser regression coverage.

Correctly applies slugs to the original ancestor path components without losing descendant directories or configured casing, and tests nested slugs, unsectioned directories, and multilingual taxonomy paths.
Correctly replaces ancestor components at their original path depths while preserving intervening directories and configured casing, with good multilingual section, taxonomy, and term coverage.
Handles the main multilingual section, taxonomy, and term cases, but rebuilding paths from ancestor basenames drops intervening directories when section parents skip directory levels.
Covers the standard cases, but once an ancestor slug changes the path, sectionSlugDir appends only each descendant branch's basename and drops any intervening non-section directories.
Fixes basic section slugs but misses descendants whose container directory extends beyond the current section, loses skipped directory components, and does not preserve unnormalized section casing.
Cleanly centralizes wrapping, updates Pretty consistently, and adds strong parser and evaluation coverage, but does not capture the actual parenthesis source bounds.

Provides a cohesive String/Pretty fix with broad regression coverage and preserved zero-literal validation, though wrapper source bounds omit the parentheses and negated wrappers still bypass that validation.
Fixes the reported round-trips and Pretty with useful parser and evaluation coverage, but duplicates literal-wrapping logic and does not capture the actual parenthesis source bounds.
Fixes String round-tripping and preserves zero/negative-literal validation with good regression tests, but leaves Pretty printing synthetic plus signs and records literal-only wrapper bounds.
Preserves the reported String outputs and accurately records direct parenthesis bounds, but omits the companion Pretty change and leaves that rendering inconsistency untested.
Fixes String round-tripping, but guesses parenthesis positions using offsets that fail with whitespace and leaves Pretty exposing the synthetic unary plus.

It has good end-to-end coverage and a mostly correct post-consolidation rewrite, but misses the lower-layer shortcut fix and execution-segment and explicit-exec edge cases while also changing an unrelated integration test.

This is a clean and well-tested core implementation across the command paths, but it can still lose scenarios during lower-layer consolidation and ignores execution-segment conflicts and raw exec-preservation semantics.

Applying the rewrite only after shortcut derivation leaves top-level execution settings intact and the patch also misses cloud-local propagation, lower-layer shortcut handling, and execution-segment conflicts.
The implementation handles basic cases but leaves default-mode shortcut fields and lower-layer settings in place, omits execution-segment conflicts, and the package suite fails.

It covers the normal run path and preserves basic scenario fields, but does not neutralize lower-layer shortcuts or handle execution-segment settings and therefore misses important consolidation edge cases.

The production logic is close to the reference and correctly handles layered consolidation, but the added tests use nonexistent Config.Once and the implementation still misses CLI execution-segment conflicts, so the package does not build.
The per-execution ReturnValue plumbing is largely sound and well tested, but the package failure indicates an unresolved edge case despite the generator update.
This is the most complete implementation and passes all supplied suites, though it should also update the fork generator and be more explicit about invalid return pipeline placement.

The sentinel implementation covers most early-return and partial-value cases, but it leaves the fork generator stale and has incomplete pipeline and template-boundary handling, as reflected by the failing package suite.
It partially works through context-captured partial returns, but bare partial output, template-call boundaries, try handling, and return propagation remain incorrect.
The separate sentinel/context path is incomplete, appears to omit the required tpl import, retains discarded-output semantics, and loses pipeline stages.
It panics with a raw ReturnError while its trap only recognizes wrapped ExecError, so normal return execution is fundamentally broken.
